title: Inclusion-Minimal local indistinguishability: a weak form of nonlocality
authors: Mao-Sheng Li, Zong-Xing Xiong, Zhu-Jun Zheng, Yan-Ling Wang
abstract: Local discrimination of quantum states is a fundamental task in distributed quantum information processing and underlies applications such as quantum communication, data hiding, and secret sharing. Here we investigate a weak form of local indistinguishability by asking how easily it can disappear when the candidate set is reduced or an additional copy of the unknown state is supplied. We introduce inclusion-minimal locally indistinguishable sets, namely, locally indistinguishable sets for which every proper subset is perfectly distinguishable by local operations and classical communication (LOCC), and show that every finite locally indistinguishable set contains such a subset. We further find that any inclusion-minimal locally indistinguishable sets becomes perfectly distinguishable by LOCC when two identical copies are available, although a single copy is insufficient. Fininally, We construct explicit inclusion-minimal locally indistinguishable product-state sets in $(\mathbb C^d)^{\otimes n}$ for every odd $d=2k+1$ and $n\ge2$. These results show that local indistinguishability can be nontrivial at the single-copy level yet fragile under either the removal of candidate states or a modest increase in copy resources, providing a complementary perspective on the structure of quantum nonlocality.
summary: This work explores 'inclusion-minimal local indistinguishability,' a weak measure of quantum nonlocality for sets of quantum states. The key finding is that such sets are fragile, as they become perfectly distinguishable by LOCC if one state is removed or if two identical copies of the state are available. The authors provide explicit constructions demonstrating this phenomenon in multipartite systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates 'local indistinguishability,' a weak form of quantum nonlocality, by analyzing how this property changes when the set of candidate quantum states is reduced or when additional copies of the unknown state are supplied.
main_result: The authors prove that inclusion-minimal locally indistinguishable sets are fragile, requiring either the deletion of a state or the availability of two identical copies to become perfectly distinguishable via Local Operations and Classical Communication (LOCC).
method: The analysis involves developing a hierarchy of concepts (inclusion-minimal vs. minimally nonlocal) and constructing explicit examples of product-state sets exhibiting this property.
model_or_system: The focus is on sets $S$ of mutually orthogonal pure quantum states, specifically product states in multipartite Hilbert spaces, analyzed under the constraints of LOCC.
key_observables: Local distinguishability, inclusion-minimal property, and $N_{LOCC}(S)$ (the minimum number of identical copies needed for LOCC discrimination).
important_parameters: Odd dimension $d=2k+1$ and the number of parties $n \ge 2$ for explicit constructions.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the framework of LOCC and assumes the states are orthogonal pure product states for the explicit constructions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the relationships between different types of nonlocal sets and schematically show the sequential measurements used to prove local distinguishability after state deletion.
paper_structure: The paper establishes definitions, proves that every finite locally indistinguishable set contains an inclusion-minimal subset, and then derives the operational consequence that such sets require two copies for LOCC discrimination, culminating in explicit constructions.
why_interesting: It provides a structural, resource-based perspective on quantum nonlocality, showing that even weak forms of nonlocality are highly sensitive to minor changes in the experimental setup (state removal or copy number).
